elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate
elements.evidence: "IBM may assign this Agreement without consent to an affiliate"

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets
elements.evidence: "or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets"

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent
elements.evidence: "MSL may not assign or transfer any rights or duties under this Agreement without prior written approval by IBM."

elements.element: Vendor consent standard: not to be unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: "without prior written approval by the other Party, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld"

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor
elements.evidence: "MSL may not assign this Agreement to any IBM competitor"

elements.element: No Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control
elements.evidence: "v) substantially all of the shares or assets of MSL are acquired by an entity that competes directly with IBM." (trigger no longer reaches an IBM change of control)

elements.element: Mutual right to assign to successors
elements.evidence: only "IBM may assign this Agreement without consent to an affiliate or to a successor"; MSL has no successor right
no notice mechanic appears; assignment carve-out is "without consent" only

elements.element: Consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: "which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld"

reasons: All five preferred atomic elements are present: Customer affiliate assignment, Customer successor assignment (merger/acquisition/sale of substantially all assets), Vendor consent requirement with a reasonableness standard, an express bar on Vendor assigning to a Customer competitor, and narrowing of trigger (v) so the competitor-acquisition exit no longer fires on an IBM change of control.

Edits are surgical: one short reasonableness qualifier, one party-name narrowing of the termination trigger, and one concise inserted sentence for the absent Customer carve-out and competitor bar — no whole-clause rewrite, no new exceptions, no boilerplate.
The fallback is separately incomplete (no mutual successor right and no written-notice mechanic), but that is irrelevable since the locked preferred level is satisfied in full.

Minor drafting nit for the rationale, not a deviation: the inserted Customer carve-out would read more cleanly opening with "Notwithstanding the foregoing," to make plain it overrides the earlier mutual consent sentence; as drafted the later specific sentence still controls and no unrelated term or defined term is disturbed.
